iOS development without a Mac: use a cloud Mac for Xcode

Reviewed: 2026-11-21 · WodeMac

Building, testing in the simulator, signing and uploading iOS apps all depend on Xcode, which only runs on macOS, so a Windows or Linux PC cannot do it directly. A common setup is to write code on your own computer and do builds and tests on a remote Mac. WodeMac rents dedicated M6 Mac minis hosted in California with admin rights, so you install Xcode yourself; under Apple's macOS license the Mac is used for software development and testing.

Why iOS development needs a Mac

Xcode runs only on macOS, and the iOS simulator, code signing, archiving and App Store Connect uploads all go through it. Cross-platform frameworks such as Flutter and React Native let you write code on Windows or Linux, but the iOS build itself still happens on a Mac.

Teams without a Mac usually buy one, borrow one or use one remotely. A remote Mac means no hardware to look after, it stays online 24/7, and teammates can connect when they need it.

Two ways to work

  • Everything on the remote desktop: open the Mac with WodeMac Remote Screen and work in Xcode and the simulator directly. Good for UI-heavy work.
  • Code locally, build remotely: develop on Windows or Linux in your usual editor and push with Git; pull on the Mac and build and test with xcodebuild, or let CI do it. Good for logic-heavy projects.

Most people mix the two: code locally, and open the remote desktop when they need to check the UI or deal with signing.

Setting up the remote Mac

  1. WodeMac helps with the first login remotely; after that you connect with WodeMac Remote Screen.
  2. Install the Xcode version your project needs from the App Store with your Apple Account, and add the platform components it asks for on first launch.
  3. Install Git, Homebrew and project dependencies such as CocoaPods, then clone the repository.
  4. Run and test the app in the simulator.
  5. Manage certificates and signing with your own Apple Developer account, then archive and upload to App Store Connect from Xcode.

Note that the Mac sits in a California data center, so you cannot plug your iPhone into it. For on-device testing, distribute builds to your own devices with TestFlight.

FAQ

Can I install Xcode on Windows?

No. Xcode only runs on macOS. You can write code on Windows and do builds, simulator tests and signing on a remote Mac.

Can I publish to the App Store from a rented Mac?

Yes. You develop, build and test on the Mac and archive and upload with your own Apple Developer account and certificates, which stay yours.

Can I debug on my own iPhone?

Not by cable, because the Mac is in a California data center. Use TestFlight to install test builds on your own devices.

Is Xcode preinstalled?

No. The WodeMac Remote Screen app is installed at delivery. Install the Xcode version your project needs from the App Store.
